        "All 524 owned diff lines across five paths were read, including both complete new source files, all five well-formed fixture generators, four tests and build registrations. HeaderBlock and stream reads force complete header buffering. FirstLine returns only LF-terminated spans, including CRLF/LF; the blank separator ends the header. EOF before a separator or a buffer beyond the configured 1 MiB limit returns an error. Buffered bytes are replayed before reading the underlying stream; the wrapper does not parse RFC fields itself.",
        "The returned header span borrows mBuffer. Once mGotHeader is true the inspected success path does not grow that vector again; keep the MailStream alive while consuming the span. HeaderBlock and EnsureHeaderInBuffer both lock mBufferMutex, matching its recursive type. This does not establish that every stream operation is thread-safe. The accepted ExchangeMessageCreate consumer is reused from C: it keeps a local RefPtr, asks for headers before any Close and parses them before streaming the full message. C remains the original reader of its whole retained consumer object.",
        "The header comment mentions calling HeaderBlock after Close. In the actual implementation Close clears mStream, and EnsureHeaderInBuffer checks that pointer before the mGotHeader loop; a new after-close HeaderBlock call therefore returns NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED even for a previously cached header. Read after close returns zero bytes with NS_OK, while Available and StreamStatus return NS_BASE_STREAM_CLOSED. This scopes the API wording; no failure was reproduced.",
        "The two positive tests compare exact header and complete-message bytes before versus after reading for CRLF, bare LF, folded headers, a large header and a large body. Two negative tests assert only isErr for a missing separator or oversized generated header. There is no explicit after-Close, short-read/error retry, cancellation or nonblocking case. All 12 added GTest assertion call sites have no streamed expected-behavior message, and both new MOZ_ASSERT(mGotHeader) calls omit an optional message. Nearby comments and task names do not supply those messages.",
